gloss: To admire fish in the water without taking action; wanting something without effort.
teaser: Ever wished for something but didn't take the leap to get it?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wished for something but didn't take the leap to get it? [break 1s] The phrase is: 临渊羡鱼, lín yuān xiàn yú. [break 0.5s] 临 (lín) - to be by; [break 0.5s] 渊 (yuān) - deep water; [break 0.5s] 羡 (xiàn) - to admire; [break 0.5s] 鱼 (yú) - fish. [break 1s] So, the full idiom is 临渊羡鱼, which literally means 'to admire fish in the deep water,' and figuratively suggests wanting something without putting in the effort to obtain it. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom comes from ancient times when people often saw fish swimming in deep waters. Many admired them from the shore, wishing to catch them, yet they never took the plunge. It highlights the idea that simply wishing for something without taking action will lead to unfulfilled desires. [break 1.5s] Here are three examples: [break 1s] 他总是临渊羡鱼，不愿意努力工作。 [break 1s] He always admires the fish in the water but is unwilling to work hard. [break 1s] 她在网上看到很多美食，却只是临渊羡鱼，没有尝试做。 [break 1s] She saw a lot of delicious food online but only admired it without trying to make it. [break 1s] 如果你想成功，就不能临渊羡鱼。 [break 1s] If you want to succeed, you can't just admire it from a distance. [break 1s] So, that's 临渊羡鱼, meaning to want something without putting in effort. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
